page_title: tapflow — Self-hosted simulator streaming for your whole team

sources.entry: tapflow - Self-hosted tool for testing iOS simulators and Android emulators from the browser, on Macs your team already owns. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jo-duchan/tapflow) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: tapflow
summary.one_liner: tapflow is an open-source, self-hosted tool that streams iOS and Android simulators and emulators to a web browser, running on Macs your team already owns.
use_cases: Let teammates test iOS apps in a browser without installing Xcode
Share Android emulators with a team over the internal network
Replace paid cloud simulator services for mobile QA
Keep app binaries and test data inside a company network
Reuse idle Mac hardware as a shared testing farm
summary.what_it_does: The page describes tapflow as a way to run iOS and Android simulators in the browser, with the simulators hosted on Macs the user controls. It states that app binaries and test data stay on the user's own network rather than going to a cloud service. It offers a single interface covering both iOS and Android simulators. The project is described as fully open source and self-hosted, released under the MIT License. The page lists setup, app testing, and operations docs in its navigation, but their content is not included in the text.
notable: Self-hosted alternative to Appetize and BrowserStack App Live
Single browser interface for both iOS simulators and Android emulators
Released under the MIT License on GitHub
Listed in awesome-mac under Developer Utilities
caveats: Runs on Macs; the page does not describe Windows or Linux hosts
Setup details are not shown in the page text, so requirements beyond owning Macs are unknown
